models_evaluated: CVD risk clinical decision support system with prioritized recommendations

links.outcome: Prescribing for CVD risk factors, CDS intervention vs control clinics
links.effect: Hypertension prescribing 34.9% with CDS use vs 34.9% control (P=.998); dyslipidemia 11.3% vs 8.7% control (P=.044); smoking cessation showed similar pattern to dyslipidemia.
links.quote: Prescribing for dyslipidemia was significantly higher at intervention encounters where the CDS system was used (11.3% [95% CI, 9.3 to 13.3]) compared with dismissed (7.7% [95% CI, 6.1 to 9.3]; P = .003) and to control encounters (8.7% [95% CI, 7.0 to 10.4]; P = .044); smoking cessation medication showed a similar pattern.

unlisted_practices: Displaying CDS recommendations prioritized by expected CVD risk-reduction benefit

models_evaluated: Cardiovascular disease risk-reduction clinical decision support system (unnamed)
unlisted_practices: Display clinical decision-support recommendations in descending order of expected benefit toward overall cardiovascular disease risk reduction.

links.effect: Hypertension prescribing was greater when CDS was used (34.9%) versus dismissed (29.6%), but showed no difference compared to control encounters (34.9%), demonstrating the necessity of randomized comparators.
links.quote: Among eligible encounters with 29,771 patients, the probability of prescribing a medication targeting hypertension was greater at intervention clinic encounters when CDS was used (34.9% [95% CI, 31.5 to 38.3]) versus dismissed (29.6% [95% CI, 26.7 to 32.6]; P < .001), but not when compared with control clinic encounters (34.9% [95% CI, 31.1 to 38.7]; P = .998).
